account:
Today there seems to be an informal effort underway that I have only partly understood. The innkeeper has arranged to meet me at eighteen hundred in the town hall great hall, describing the occasion as a community meal. My neighbour said the innkeeper was raising sixteen emeralds for bread, and the secretary reports that the builder mentioned funding shortages. The neighbour corrected my impression that the builder wanted a private meeting with me: apparently the builder wanted the innkeeper. I also saw the innkeeper give the baker a lantern this morning. These things might be connected with providing the meal, but I do not yet know the precise arrangements or whether any help is expected from me.

Several townsfolk near the bakery repeated the peculiar phrase 'bridge or port change at bakery.' None supplied an explanation or firsthand confirmation. I cannot treat that as evidence that a bridge or port change is actually planned. Freight has explicitly said no town assistance is needed for warehouse coordination, so I should not assume that activity is a problem or part of the meal.

My grain inspection did not happen this morning because I could not locate the miller. I asked the secretary to arrange tomorrow at ten, subject to the miller's availability, although her subsequent question suggests that the arrangement still needs clear confirmation. There were no new council letters when I attended the office. I have now arrived early for my fifteen hundred tea with the neighbour, who is here waiting. This is a chance to learn firsthand what the meal and fundraising are for, rather than build conclusions out of repeated rumours. My present guess is that people are coordinating a community meal with some difficulty funding bread, not that I have established any secret scheme.
